thread:
monitor-bot: ALERT: sustained p99 latency > 2.0s on cluster shared-gpu-pool (streaming path). Auto-page: sre-oncall-priya. Links: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/alerts/2876549999 :rotating_light:

sre-oncall-priya: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 600ms, p99 spikes to 2-3s for the last 6m. Streaming stalls and partial responses reported. Starting initial triage.

alice-prod: hitting customer reports too — customer: openai-tools (tenant-114) seeing degraded playback and partial streams. They're on a dedicated group but still routed through shared pool for burst.

mike-runtime: adding context: recent autoscaler bump earlier today added 6 more pods to shared-gpu-pool, but I see high IO wait on GPUs and host NVMe. Could be noisy tenant.

jordan-ml: any model changes deployed in last hour? Rollouts?

sre-oncall-priya: checked model-rollouts: none in prod in last 3h. No config changes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new nodepool autoscaled: +6 nodes to pool/shared-gpu (reason: load). Deploy link: https://deploys/redwood/4567

alice-prod: logs from edge show repeated streaming stall frames with "write stalled" and backend chunk timeouts. Sample log:
```
streaming: send_chunk id=abcd123 len=1024ms attempt=1 error=write_timeout
rpc: deadline exceeded while sending chunk to connection tenant=114
```

mike-runtime: running quick `top` and `iostat` on affected host (gpu-node-17):
```
$ ssh gpu-node-17
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  %util
nvme0n1          12.0   850.0  1024.0 24576.0  120.5  98.9
```
High NVMe write bandwidth, %util ~99.

jordan-ml: suggests noisy neighbor doing large streaming writes to disk (caching or checkpointing). Could be KV cache evictions writing to disk?

sre-oncall-priya: paging oncall-mike-runtime and alice-prod for mitigation. Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle IO for top containers via cgroups/ionice, 2) migrate suspected tenant pods off shared pool to burst-isolated pool, 3) enable fallback to smaller-model variant for affected customers.

alice-prod: customer-impact list: openai-tools (tenant-114) streaming stalls, 3 support tickets opened; second customer (tenant-203) intermittent p99 spikes. Mark as user-facing and SLO assessment required.

mike-runtime: I can identify top IO processes with `iotop -aoP` and then apply `cgcreate`/`cgset` limits or `ionice -c3` to deprioritize.

jordan-ml: also check GPU utilization and NVLink traffic: `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nvidia-smi topo -m` — if GPU compute is fine but host IO is saturated it's definitely NVMe.

sre-oncall-priya: mike, go ahead with identification. I'll notify cust-success and mark incident. Anne @cust-success-anne can you send a short note to impacted customers with ETA?

cust-success-anne: on it. Short message ready: "We're investigating streaming latency; temporary mitigation underway. No data loss; will update in 20m." Sending now.

mike-runtime: found top consumers via `iotop`:
```
PID  USER   DISK READ  DISK WRITE  COMMAND
22411 svc-tn114 0.00 K/s  180MB/s  /usr/bin/redis-checkpoint --tenant=114
33210 svc-tn203 0.00 K/s  95MB/s   /usr/bin/cache-evictor --shard=3
```
Looks like tenant-114's periodic checkpoint kicked off heavy writes.

alice-prod: tenant-114 has checkpoint config set to local NVMe backup for faster recovery; that explains heavy writes. We should avoid local NVMe writes during shared peak.

mike-runtime: applying a low-priority IO class to tenant-114 containers as quick mitigation:
```
# find container pid for tenant-114
pid=22411
# set ionice to idle
sudo nsenter -t $pid -n ionice -c3 -p $pid
# for cgroups v1 example
sudo cgcreate -g blkio:/tenant114
sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.write_bps_device="8:0 150000000" tenant114
sudo cgclassify -g blkio:tenant114 $pid
```
Applying now.

infra-bot: action: cgroup throttle applied to tenant-114 on gpu-node-17 by mike-runtime.

alice-prod: immediate telemetry shows p99 falling from ~2.5s to ~700ms within 30s of throttle. p95 steady ~550ms. Partial improvement but still above SLO.

jordan-ml: good. Next, migrate tenant-114 to isolation pool for the remainder of the peak window. That reduces risk of repeated checkpoint during busy hours.

sre-oncall-priya: mike, can you trigger a live migration (kubectl cordon/drain of pods)? Use burst-isolation-pool nodes.

mike-runtime: performing pod migration now:
```
# label nodes
kubectl get pods -l tenant=114 -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl delete {}
# rely on HPA/controller to recreate in pool with nodeSelector: pool=burst-isolation
```
Migration started.

alice-prod: while migrating, a few streams will reconnect. Customer-facing degradation window ~2-4m. Anne, update customers: migration in progress, expect resolution in <10m.

cust-success-anne: updated. customers acknowledged.

mike-runtime: migration completed. tenant-114 pods now on nodes labeled pool=burst-isolation (gpu-node-27, gpu-node-28). Verifying IO on gpu-node-17: `iostat` now:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  %util
nvme0n1           2.0    12.0   128.0  2048.0   5.3   12.1
```
NVMe utilization back to normal.

alice-prod: p99 down to 380ms, p95 180ms across streaming routes. Looks like full mitigation.

jordan-ml: please note: tenant checkpoint config should be updated to use network-backed object store for checkpoints (S3) or rate-limited writes when on shared pools. We'll recommend config change in follow-up.

sre-oncall-priya: marking incident as mitigated. Creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem: owner mike-runtime, reviewers alice-prod and jordan-ml.

mike-runtime: immediate followups I'll include in postmortem: 1) change default checkpoint strategy for tenants on shared pool, 2) add automatic detection of heavy host NVMe writes and apply auto-ionice + migration policy, 3) add runbook for cgroup throttle and migration.

alice-prod: ask product: consider a tenant QoS tag to prevent local NVMe checkpoints on shared pools automatically.

cust-success-anne: I'll follow up with impacted customers with final incident summary and timeline once postmortem is ready.

infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-0315-2876549999 assigned_to: mike-runtime severity: P2 impact: degraded streaming latency for tenants 114,203.

sre-oncall-priya: thanks team. Leaving notes here: observed noisy neighbor (checkpoint) -> IO saturation -> streaming stalls. Mitigated by cgroup throttle + live migration to isolation pool. Next: automate detection + preventative configuration. I'll handoff to oncall-mike for postmortem.

mike-runtime: will do. If anyone sees residual anomalies ping me.

jordan-ml: suggest adding a metric for host NVMe %util per pool and an alert at 85% to preempt this.

alice-prod: agreed. Adding to postmortem action items.

cust-success-anne: customers acknowledged and appreciate rapid mitigation. Closing external comms after the postmortem.

monitor-bot: INFO: alert resolved for rule shared-gpu-pool-high-p99 at 2876551459.

sre-oncall-priya: closing thread. Postmortem draft expected EOD. :white_check_mark:
